operations.np.add.reduce: numpy/_core/src/umath/loops_utils.h.src DOUBLE_pairwise_sum (n < 8: serial from -0.0; n <= 128: 8 accumulators, ((r0+r1)+(r2+r3))+((r4+r5)+(r6+r7)), serial tail; else split at n2 = n/2 - (n/2) % 8) added to the identity 0.0

tolerance_classes.EXACT_VALUE: integers, strings, enums, statuses, exception classes and messages, and floats that are copied (not computed): equal; floats compared bitwise except NaN == NaN
tolerance_classes.ULP_BOUNDED: per observable above. ulp(x) = 2^(floor(log2 |x|) - 52) for normal x (subnormal / zero: 2^-1074). A relative clause is scaled by |py| (not max(1, |py|): rates are ~1e-13..1e-40 m^3/s, an absolute floor of r_rel would accept nonsense)
tolerance_classes.EXACT_STREAM: not used (no RNG in either implementation)

tolerance_basis.independence: fixed from an a priori floating-point analysis of the two registered algorithms before any Rust code or Python-vs-Rust comparison existed; the only measurements used are properties of the inputs (table sizes, ranges, signs) and of the reference environment (numpy algorithms and dispatch read from source; three numpy routines confirmed bitwise against pure-Python emulations)
tolerance_basis.which_operations_differ: identical in both (expected bit-identical): grid construction (linspace, sorted unique), np.interp (X86_V2 baseline, no FMA), -grid / T_e, sg * grid, the trapezoid terms, the pairwise sum and its order, QE**2, sqrt(8 / (pi m_e)), (QE T_e)**-1.5 (glibc pow in CPython float_pow, numpy npy_pow and Rust powf), the final products, every scalar operation of step_cross_section_rate (glibc sqrt / exp in CPython math and Rust std) and of tail_sensitivity. Different: the float64 exp of the integrand array: numpy SVML __svml_exp8_ha against glibc exp; bound registered as <= 4 ulp for numpy (the SIMD transcendental bound used by the earlier ES-2 contracts; SVML 'ha' is documented < 1 ulp) and < 1 ulp for glibc, i.e. <= 5 ulp between them
tolerance_basis.maxwellian_rate_bound: u = 2^-53. Inputs E >= 0, sigma >= 0 finite. Interpolation: numpy's search returns j with xp[j] <= x < xp[j+1] for every key (also for non-monotonic xp: every return path tests both inequalities), so sg is a convex combination of non-negative sigma values (negative only by O(u) rounding when one end is 0) and every integrand y_i >= 0 up to O(u). Per element: |y_r - y_p| <= (10u + 2u) y = 12u y (exp difference + the two product roundings). Trapezoid term t_i = (d_i (y_{i+1} + y_i)) / 2: +2u for the sum, +2u for the product, /2 exact: 16u. Pairwise sum of n <= 22203 terms (grid <= 20000 + 2202 + 2 points): rounding depth D <= 33 (<= 8 recursion levels for n < 32768, <= 15 accumulator additions + 3 combination levels + 7 tail additions in a 128-block); two identical summation trees with perturbed non-negative inputs differ by <= (16u + 2 gamma_33) S = (16 + 66) u S. Times QE^2 and times the identical prefactor: +2u each. Total: |k_r - k_p| <= 86 u |k_p| = 9.5e-15 |k_p|. Registered r_rel = 1e-13 (about 10x the worst case; the expected difference is a few ulp)
tolerance_basis.subnormal_clause: the relative bound assumes normal intermediates. Terms with a subnormal exp have y_i = p_i e_i < 2.2e-322 (p_i = sigma E <= 1e-14) and carry absolute errors of a few 2^-1074; the integral (trapezoid * QE^2 = 2.57e-38 * S) can be subnormal when S < 8.6e-271, where rounding to the subnormal grid changes it by one quantum 2^-1074. Mapped through the prefactor sqrt(8/(pi m_e)) (e T_e)^-1.5 <= 2.6e46 for T_e >= 0.01 eV, that quantum is <= 1.3e-277 m^3/s; registered a_abs = 1e-250 m^3/s covers it with margin for every registered T_e >= 0.01 eV and lies > 200 orders of magnitude below any physical rate coefficient
tolerance_basis.tail_sensitivity_bound: share = (a - b) / a with a = k_hold, b = k_zero, each within rho = 9.5e-15 relative (above), 0 <= b <= 2a on the registered inputs: |delta share| <= rho (a + b) / a + rho |share| + 2u <= 3 rho + 2u; registered 4e-13 = 3 r_rel + margin. The registered eps >= 3 eV (T_e >= 2 eV) keeps every k_hold of the registered tables far above the subnormal range (smallest: TAB-06 at T_e = 2 eV, ~1e-33 m^3/s)
tolerance_basis.step_bound: every operation is the same correctly rounded IEEE operation or the same glibc call in the same order: expected bit-identical; k_ulp = 1
tolerance_basis.table_text_bound: the formatter is checked separately (render, strictly EXACT_BYTES); a table line can then differ only through the row-k difference crossing a 7-significant-digit rounding boundary, which the BOUNDARY_ROUNDING rule detects exactly

mapping.rule: the reference API returns abep_types::pyjson::PyException {class, message} with Python's class and message; converted to abep_types::AbepError it is AbepError::OutOfDomain (status OUT_OF_DOMAIN) for every class: each mirrors an argument outside the function's domain

domain_and_error_parity.mapping_rule: every Python exception class used by the component maps to exactly one Rust error variant / status; no Rust path returns a value where Python raises, or raises where Python returns, except the documented divergences below (CLAUDE.md rule 3: no silent fallbacks)

documented_divergence.statement: non-finite table entries (NaN / +-inf in E_eV or sigma_m2): Python propagates them through numpy (NaN or garbage results with RuntimeWarnings); the Rust reference API refuses with OUT_OF_DOMAIN before computing
documented_divergence.disposition: fail closed (rule 3); outside the registered parity domain; DE-25 / DE-26 pass when Rust refuses (Python's outcome is recorded, not compared)

documented_divergence.statement: write_hallthruster_table with a finite eps_max > 1e6 eV: Python allocates and integrates O(eps_max) rows, or raises MemoryError depending on host memory; Rust refuses with OUT_OF_DOMAIN (writer domain: eps_max <= 1e6 eV, NaN / +-inf / lengths outside intp mirrored as Python's ValueError)
documented_divergence.disposition: fail closed; DE-W7 passes when Rust refuses

documented_divergence.statement: the checked API (abep_chem::checked) has no Python counterpart: where the reference silently holds the last cross section beyond the table (tail 'hold'), returns 0.0 for T_e <= 0, NaN for non-finite T_e, or accepts a representation that is empty, mismatched, non-finite, negative or decreasing, the checked API refuses: rate_validity semantics (CLAUDE.md next-work 5, NP-ICP-CHEM-AIR IX-04..IX-06) -> OUT_OF_DOMAIN beyond max_mean_energy_eV, INCOMPLETE_EVIDENCE for 'unresolved', MODEL_ERROR for a missing entry or an invalid representation; OUT_OF_DOMAIN for T_e not finite and > 0 or an unrepresentable prefactor
documented_divergence.disposition: production consumers (abep-icp, IF-CHEM-REG-v1) call the checked API; the reference API exists for parity and for byte-identical table rebuilds; INV-06 verifies the checked semantics

documented_divergence.statement: argument typing: Python accepts any array-like / int arguments (an int threshold is printed as an int, e.g. '15'); the Rust API takes f64 slices and f64 scalars. All registered thresholds and every harness argument are Python floats
numpy RuntimeWarnings (overflow / invalid value) are not reproduced: they are warnings, not results

finite negative E_eV or sigma_m2 values are computed by the reference API with the same operation sequence as Python but lie outside the registered parity domain (no vector draws them; the error analysis assumes E, sigma >= 0); no admission claim covers them

decision_rules.per_test: every scored observable of every vector meets its tolerance class; every outcome (value / exception class and message) is EXACT_VALUE-equal, except DIV-01 / DIV-02 cases, which pass only when Rust refuses with OUT_OF_DOMAIN
decision_rules.verdict: ADMITTED iff every per-test, invariant (INV-01, INV-03..INV-06; INV-02 is an input precondition), domain/error and schema check passes and every reference file matches sha256_at_registration; PARITY_PASS <=> ADMITTED, PARITY_FAIL <=> NOT_ADMITTED
decision_rules.meaning_of_ADMITTED: A9.24 item 1: Rust becomes authoritative for this component (within the registered domain); new production results for it come from Rust and carry implementation = rust, rust_commit and this contract id; the Python component may then be retired from active execution. It is NOT physics validation. For NP-ICP-NEUTRALIZER it satisfies software_admission item (3) ('the abep-chem rate evaluator it uses is admitted'); it does not admit any table, registry or validity entry (NP-ICP-CHEM-AIR)
decision_rules.no_retuning: tolerances, observables, inputs, n, seeds and rules are fixed; after NOT_ADMITTED only a code fix plus a new contract version with a fresh scoring_master_seed may follow; the failed report stays; no execution is discarded
decision_rules.disagreement_rule: never rewrite a Python result, golden, fixture or frozen dataset to make Rust pass (RM-R11)

decision_rules.scoring_once: the scoring comparison runs once (scoring_master_seed); the harness refuses a second scoring run when parity_report_v1.json exists, a reference or input pin differs, or a Rust / harness provenance source is uncommitted; development runs (development_master_seed) never write a report into the contract directory
